final_rationale: The verdict did not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence; the response mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and made concessions that align with the initial audit concerns. That narrowing is useful, but it does not cure the core compliance gap. On the present record, aggregate launch readiness may be supportable, yet the claim being audited was compliance of certification without treating the known segment-specific gap as a material weakness requiring disclosure or approved risk acceptance. The policy text says a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the available evidence summary still places this segment in named pilot commitments while legal review remains open. Because no disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or resolution was added, the unresolved caveat is still an unmet compliance predicate rather than a harmless qualification. That keeps the claim suspicious rather than moving it to compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided to resolve whether the mortgage servicing assistant gap is a material weakness under the policy text.
The available record still indicates the affected segment is tied to named servicer pilot commitments, which keeps the materiality predicate live.
No disclosure text, approved risk acceptance, or issue resolution was produced, even though one of those appears required if the weakness is material.
Pending legal review still weighs against treating the issue as resolved.
Aggregate pass metrics and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not satisfy the specific disclosure/materiality requirement.
